key_insight: Higher-order parity constraints can improve QAOA success probabilities beyond addressing hardware connectivity, apparently by accelerating correlation propagation.
engineering_relevance: Parity-based QAOA offers a promising route to better optimization on quantum hardware using parameters trained on smaller instances.
method: Apply selected parity transformations to Signed Max-Cut on 3-regular graphs.
Classically optimize QAOA parameters on training instances with up to 14 vertices, then transfer them to larger instances.
Evaluate parity-based and conventional QAOA on IBM Heron processors, incorporating error mitigation.
evidence_signal: With error mitigation, parity-based QAOA found optimal solutions for all tested 40-vertex instances, whereas conventional QAOA failed under the same conditions.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested problem family and instances; broader scaling and robustness to hardware noise remain to be established.
paper_title: Higher-order Parity Constraints for Quantum Approximate Optimization
